specification.problem: Quantum approximate optimization (QAOA) for combinatorial optimization with an integer depth parameter p>=1; approximation quality improves with p. Studied on MaxCut for regular graphs, with analysis for 2-regular and 3-regular graphs at fixed p. For p=1 on 3-regular graphs the cut is at least 0.6924 times the optimum.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small finite instance: MaxCut on a regular graph (e.g. 3-regular) at p=1. Only the abstract-level structure is reconstructed; the explicit gate forms, angle optimization and the 0.6924 derivation are not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Objective as sum of clauses
equations.description: Objective function is a sum over m constraints, each of limited locality.
equations.justification: The abstract refers to the objective's locality and a number of constraints; the sum form is inferred.
assumptions: Each C_alpha acts on a bounded number of bits

equations.label: Depth scaling
equations.description: Circuit depth grows linearly with p times at worst the number of constraints m.
equations.abstract_quote: The depth of the circuit grows linearly with $p$ times (at worst) the number of constraints.

equations.label: Approximation ratio at p=1
equations.description: For p=1 on 3-regular graphs the found cut is at least 0.6924 of the optimum.
equations.abstract_quote: For $p=1$, on 3-regular graphs the quantum algorithm always finds a cut that is at least 0.6924 times the size of the optimal cut.

equations.label: Variational state
equations.description: Standard QAOA state with phase-separation and mixing layers; the form is not stated in the abstract.
equations.justification: Standard QAOA form, assumed to match the paper's algorithm.

registers.name: q
registers.role: Computational register encoding the bit string z; the cut is read from it

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition |+>^{\otimes n} (assumed standard QAOA initial state)

steps.description: Prepare |+>^{\otimes n} by applying Hadamard to each qubit.
For each layer l=1..p, apply phase-separation unitary e^{-i gamma_l C}, a product of gates of locality at most that of each clause (two-qubit ZZ phases per edge for MaxCut).
In each layer apply the mixing unitary e^{-i beta_l B} with single-qubit X rotations on all qubits.
Total depth scales as O(p m) with m constraints; for p=1 on 3-regular graphs the target guarantee is ratio >=0.6924.

specification.measurement: Measure all n qubits in the computational (Z) basis to obtain a bit string z; repeat preparation and measurement many times to estimate <C> and to sample candidate cuts.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate C(z) classically for each sampled string and keep the best cut. For fixed p, angles (gamma,beta) are chosen by classical preprocessing/optimization of <gamma,beta|C|gamma,beta> (procedure not given in abstract).
assumptions: The state form in eq_4 is standard QAOA background, not taken from the abstract.
Registers, initial state and mixer are assumed standard QAOA choices.
Measurement in the computational basis with best-of-samples postprocessing is assumed standard QAOA practice.
